Here’s a classic, fool‑proof list of ingredients for a moist, chocolate‑y cake that’s perfect for birthdays, parties, or a cozy Sunday treat. Feel free to tweak quantities or add extras (like espresso powder or a splash of orange liqueur) to suit your taste. | Ingredient | Quantity (for a 9‑inch round cake, 2 layers) | Notes | |------------|---------------------------------------------|-------| | All‑purpose flour | 1 ¾ cups (220 g) | Sifted, or sift and whisk to remove lumps. | | Unsweetened cocoa powder | ¾ cup (75 g) | Use a high‑quality Dutch‑process cocoa for richer flavor. | | Granulated sugar | 2 cups (400 g) | White sugar gives a clean sweetness; you can swap half for brown sugar for a deeper flavor. | | Baking powder | 1 ½ tsp | Helps the cake rise; make sure it’s fresh. | | Baking soda | 1 ½ tsp | Works with the acidity of the cocoa and buttermilk. | | Salt | ½ tsp | Enhances all the flavors. | | Eggs | 2 large | Room temperature for better emulsion. | | Whole milk | 1 cup (240 ml) | Room temperature; can replace with buttermilk for extra tenderness. | | Vegetable oil | ½ cup (120 ml) | Neutral oil keeps the cake moist; can use melted butter for richer flavor. | | Vanilla extract | 2 tsp | Pure vanilla for depth. | | Boiling water | 1 cup (240 ml) | Hot water dissolves cocoa and flour, creating a silky batter. | | Optional extras | | • 1 tsp espresso powder (boosts chocolate flavor)
• ¼ cup chocolate chips or chopped nuts (for texture)
• 1 tbsp cocoa‑flavored liqueur (for an adult twist) | ### Quick Tips - **Sift dry ingredients** together first; this ensures even distribution of leavening agents and cocoa. - **Cream the butter (or oil) and sugar** until light and fluffy before adding eggs; this incorporates air for a lighter crumb. - **Add eggs one at a time**, mixing well after each addition to keep the batter smooth. - **Fold in the dry mix** gently, then pour in the hot water last—this helps the batter stay airy. - **Bake at 350 °F (175 °C)** for about 30–35 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out clean. - **Cool in the pan for 10 min**, then turn onto a wire rack to finish cooling. Enjoy your chocolate cake! If you’d like a frosting recipe or variations, just let me know.
